This is the 50 largest one-day backwardation value seen since August 2008, 40 and the deepest sustained move into backwardation since mid2008. Just before the 2008 crisis broke, supply was severely 30 disrupted by a number of mine strikes and stocks were low, 20 meaning concerns about the immediate availability of metal 10 kept the market in backwardation. As the crisis resulted in an increase in availability of prompt material, the forward curve 0 moved into contango throughout by year-end. This time -10 around, we are seeing some degree of supply disruption, but -20 not to the same extent as in Q2 2008. We believe that the underlyin

g reason behind the disparity in stock levels has been that a lot of material is fundamentally in the wrong location, as Western demand was not as depressed as many had initially feared while Chinese demand has so far turned out to be much lower than most people’s expectations for this year. However, the tightness seen outside China has been exacerbated by the high levels of warrant cancellations in LME warehouses in the last few months. While some of this material may have gone into China, trade data indicate that most of it could not have done. The cancellation levels have also been too high for the remaining material to have been consumed, and so it seems likely that much of the material has gone or is destined to go into private warehouses. The high levels of cancellations have also created short term scarcity of physical metal, as queues have lengthened to deliver metal out of LME warehouses. This drives up spot cathode premia and prices for prompt delivery, resulting in the backwardation we are seeing. It is not clear whether the backwardation is side-effect of a drive amongst certain market players to boost premia, or the desired result: Physical scarcity boosts premia, thus benefiting anyone holding copper cathode. A backwardation can also benefit a holder of metal, as they can lend it to the market by selling cash and buying it back further forward. Realistically, it is probably a combination of both. In the last month, the level of cancelled warrants in LME warehouses was declining as material cancelled earlier was delivered out. However, a sudden raft of cancellations in warehouses around the world on 20th April moved over 40,000t off-warrant, boosting the LME cash price and driving a wider backwardation situation. This global inventory cancellation which affected six warehouse locations in five countries © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 18 Copper Monitor May 2012 www. crugroup.com was the biggest one-day change ever, and happened to occur on the Friday following the copper market’s annual CESCO week get-together and CRU conference in Santiago. #### Copper price falters and rebounds in April Long liquidation and short

The copper price moved down in the first half of April, having covering in April held in a relatively narrow band of $8,200-8,700/t since late LME open interest vs average, Oct ‘11 – Apr ‘12 January, due to worries over the global economy and Chinese Contracts demand. European debt concerns flared up again, with a 340,000 disappointing debt a

uction by the Spanish government and the 330,000 LME Open Interest 5D MA release of gloomy retail and business activity data for February, 320,000 LME Cash 5D MA while the US outlook cooled on lower than expected jobs 310,000 growth data and the failure of the Federal Reserve to announce 300,000 another stimulus package.  Further downward pressure was 290,000 applied to the price by the increasing apprehension in the 280,000 market over Chinese demand growth prospects for 2012. 270,000 Indeed, in our conversations with market participants during 260,000 CESCO week, the general consensus was of weaker than 250,000 expected demand in China in Q2.  If we compare the five-day 240,000 Oct 11 Dec 11 Feb 12 moving averages of open interest against the cash price on the Data: LME LME during mid-April (see accompanying chart), the falling price coupled with net reductions in open positions indicate a tendency towards liquidation of long positions at that time. 

However, prices steadied during CESCO week as market players found themselves in broad agreement over a resurgence of Chinese demand in H2, while weaker preliminary Q1 supply data bolstered support. The simultaneous warrant cancellations on 20<sup>th</sup> April, discussed above, squeezed near-term availability outside China during the following week.  With open interest falling at the same time, it appears that the squeeze has precipitated a round of short covering, which kick-started a rebound in prices. 

#### China stock build eases 

In the face of a weaker than expected start to the year, many are questioning the outlook Chinese demand in 2012.  That stock levels are very high is not disputed, and stories abound of idled mills and reduced orders for cathode from Chinese semi-fabricators.  While many believe that around 80-90% of the estimated 600,000t of stocks in Shanghai bonded warehouses are being utilised for financing purposes, there are still numerous signs that stocks are too high for physical requirements.  A number of exporters of cathode to China tell us that they have received requests from customers to delay shipments, and there have been incidences of material headed for China being diverted to Europe.  The significant negative arbitrage between LME and SHFE has encouraged a few traders to engage in re-exporting cathode to Asian LME warehouses, and earlier this week, a number of Chinese smelters including Jiangxi Copper announced a joint agreement to deliver cathode to the LME over the next two months, ostensibly to ease tightness in the global market.  (We note that this is only possible due to the tolling regulations introduced

However, the course of the Chinese market

is beginning to turn. Consumption is set to pick up in Q2 by around 13%, mainly due to seasonal working patterns. We understand that many of the semi-fabricators have only booked 60% of their annual requirements, implying that they will have to enter the spot market at some point, supporting demand. From a macroeconomic perspective, China’s latest official manufacturing PMI showed a reading of 53.3 for April, up from 53.1 in March, which, if not overwhelmingly bullish, is positive for growth prospects. Finally, stock levels have begun to stabilise: Last week’s SHFE total of just under 205,000t represented a decline of 9.9% from the peak of 227,000t on 16th March. Moreover, we are informed that the build-up in bonded stocks has slowed. In our last Monitor, we wrote that Chinese refined imports would decline in March due to increased domestic production, mediocre consumption, high bonded stocks and low premia, and imports did fall by 8% to just under 345,000t. This gives total first quarter imports at a record level of 1.06Mt – an increase of just 1.1% compared to the previous quarter, but a massive 78.6% increase compared to Q1 2011. So, despite the second consecutive record quarterly cathode imports and a slight increase in production so far this year, it appears that the stock build ran out of steam in April. We therefore believe that the expected pickup in consumption in Q2 is beginning to materialise. Looking ahead, while bonded stocks remain at high levels, the unfavourable SHFE/LME arbitrage will continue to discourage spot import activity, and following our expectations that consumption will grow by more than production, stocks should begin to be drawn down. #### Early Q1 supply data down Q1 supply results are beginning to come in, and the details of a number of disruptions have been revealed. CRU production forecasts already take into account the higher likelihood of weather-related disturbances in Q1, due to the occurrence of the rainy season in Queensland, the African Copperbelt and the Atacama desert in Chile and Peru, as well as winter in the northern hemisphere. Chinese output is expected to be disrupted at all points of the supply chain due to the New Year holiday. We also note that Q1 is the start of the calendar year, and the quarter which - in many cases - inspires the least consideration amongst workers for annual production targets. At this stage, we know that heavy rains disrupted the Collahuasi and Tintaya mines, technical problems beset at least three smelters causing outages, and ore grades were lower than expected at Bingham Canyon. However, ramping up continues at the Los Bronces and Antamina brownfield expansion projects, offsetting some of the production losses elsewhere. Given the above, we see refined output amounting to around 4.7Mt in the first quarter of the year, down 4.4% compared to the previous quarter and almost 0.6% higher than a year earlier. Output is expected to pick up from Q2 as extreme weather conditions recede and as Chinese productivity improves following its holiday-interrupted first quarter. However, output growth is not expected to come close to meeting consumption increases in Q2, so our refined deficit is projected to grow from around 20,000t in Q1 to 330,000t in Q2, with much of the latter expected to be met by the drawdown in Chinese stocks. In H2, we see flat production growth in Q3 and an increase in Q4, as mine, smelter and refinery workers push to meet calendar year targets. #### Al rod market tightness shows In our February monitor, we observed that the recent closures of aluminium production units, mainly due to low prices and oversupply, would lead to a shortage of aluminium rod. We are beginning to see evidence of this: Recent media reports quote US wire and cable producers as saying that they have been forced to increase expenditure by sourcing rod outside the US, due to two smelter outages in the country, and imports of aluminium rod, bar and profile were up 25% y-o-y in February into the US. While we have yet to hear that the wire and cable plants have turned to copper rod as a substitute due to the scarcity of aluminium rod, it remains a possibility if the situation persists. At the very least this reduces the possibility of substitution losses from copper rod to aluminium. #### Price testing downside support The uncertain start to April saw the 3-month LME price test but fail to break below the short term uptrend line of $7,900/t, after which it seems that short-covering has driven the price rebound seen in recent days. While the squeeze on LME stocks has exerted more upward pressure on the cash price, driving the backwardation, the 3-month price has also moved up strongly, implying underlying support for prices above $8,000/t. As the chart indicates, the 3-month price has recently breached the 100-day and now the 30-day moving averages. At the time of going to press, the price had approached and retreated from $8,400 and was looking ready to test $8,200/t on the way down. If this level is breached we would expect the next test to be at $7,900/t, where we anticipate firm support as stocks are drawn down and sentiments improve as evidence of higher seasonal demand materialises. The difficulties in the Chinese wirerod market were strongly felt in North East Asia in Q1 2012, where production of copper wirerod shrank by 3.7% y-o-y in the period. South Korea was the region most severely affected, with production falling by 7.8% y-o-y, whereas, Taiwan recorded a 3.7% decline. It was also reported that wire and cable production in Vietnam fell by 19.1%. Production in Japan remained largely flat, supported by a rebounding domestic construction sector and strong industrial growth. However, much of this growth was due to the weak conditions in the comparable period in 2011, following the natural disasters that struck in March 2011. Chinese production of wirerod increased to 1.265Mt in Q1 2012, up by 5.2% y-o-y. There have been few announcements of new projects coming on in the region. The only major development in the past three months is the beginning of construction work at **Wuxi Lineo Science and Technology Group** ’s 60,000t/y copper wirerod mill in Jiangsu province. Start-up is expected to take place by October 2012. The company will also invest in a second phase expansion project that will involve the addition of another 60,000t/y wirerod production line by November 2014. The plant will be primarily fed with refined copper cathode sourced from **Tongling Nonferrous Metals** in Anhui province and is designed to serve domestic wire and cable producers © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 10 of 18 Copper Monitor May 2012 www

. crugroup.com unless market prices become sufficiently attractive to allow for export. Wuxi Lineo Group is a private enterprise with downstream manufacturing subsidiaries producing cable, hardware, mechanical and electrical products. In other developments, it was reported that in February Japan’s **Furukawa Electric** introduced a 500t/y copper wirerod production line at its subsidiary, **Shenyang Furukawa Cable** in China. The wirerod is used to produce conductors, which were previously purchased from outside the company. The development of the production line is part of Furukawa's move to shift more production in-house. #### Renewed optimism in the Americas World Cu wirerod consumption

Consumption of copper wirerod in the US strengthened in Q1 2012, growing by 2.7% y-o-y to 327,000t. This compares to a decline of 0.2% in Q1 2011. Although business conditions remain difficult in the US due to the depressed construction sector, the negative trend for housing permits appears to have stabilised at a low level and is not expected to decline further. Meanwhile, the automotive sector is performing well and is supporting copper wirerod consumption, which has further benefitted from a return of consumer confidence and demand from the industrial sectors. US production of copper wirerod also increased in Q1 2012, 12.6% ROW 17.8% rising by 2.8% to 342,000t. This is set to grow further in the imminent future with the expected commissioning of **SDI LaFarga LLC** ’s 82,000t/y copper wirerod plant in New **Data: CRU** Haven, Indiana, this month. The plant is expected to reach 70% utilisation before the end of 2012. The joint venture company involves the merged interests of US-based carbon steel producer and scrap metal recycler, **Steel Dynamic’s Inc.** and Spain-based copper semis fabricator, **LaFarga Group** . The facility will consume copper scrap in its production process, with the majority likely to consist of No. 2 copper scrap from Steel Dynamic’s scrap processing facility, **OmniSource Corp** . The use of anything other than the highest grade copper scrap is unprecedented in the US wirerod market and SDI LaFarga’s facility will therefore function as a unique new area of demand for No. 2 copper scrap in the US. This will decrease the availability of US No. 2 scrap for export to China and should narrow scrap discounts. We have also seen promising signs of growth in the Brazilian wirerod sector, with consumption of copper wirerod increasing by 2.4% y-o-y in Q1 2012. Much of the growth came from the government’s reduction to its inflation-mitigating interest rates, which encouraged economic growth. Our forecast for Brazilian cathode c

onsumption in 2012 is for a rise of 6% y-o-y, outperforming the increase in industrial production due to copper demand’s heavy exposure to essential infrastructure developments related to the 2014 World Cup hosted in Brazil. Moreover, production of copper wirerod rose by 19.6% in the same period, marking the region as a net producer of the material. Previously, shortages in domestic production were made up through © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 11 of 18 Copper Monitor May 2012 www.crugroup.com imports of wirerod from nearby Chile. Much of the growth in production is attributed to the Rio de Janeiro State Government’s introduction of a tax incentive plan to initiate and promote the growth of the downstream copper industry. Most recently, the reduction in the VAT on copper products from 19% to 2% (only eligible for companies investing over R$40M) has led to a decision by **Ibrame** , the Brazilian manufacturer of copper cathode, wirerod, bar and other products, to construct a copper rod mill in Itatiaia. Upon commissioning in early 2013, the facility is initially expected to produce 70,000t/y of wirerod, processed mainly from direct-use scrap, with capacity rising to 100,000t/y in subsequent years. #### Russia’s transition to wirerod exports plateaus We estimate that Russian copper wirerod production rose by 213,000t or 44% y-o-y to reach 698,000t in 2011 on the back of export duties on cathode imposed in November 2010. The production increase in Q1 2012 was, however, less marked, as we believe that the transition from cathode exports to copper wirerod exports was nearing completion by the end of 2011. Nonetheless, **Russkaya Mednaya Kompaniya** ’s (RMK) **Kyshtym Electrolytic Copper** wirerod plant (JSC ‘KMEZ’) in the Chelyabinsk region is undergoing development and modernisation work, which involved an investment of 144M roubles (US$4.8M) in 2011 and is expected to require at least a further 170M roubles (US$5.6M) in 2012. RMK stated that it will invest 19.0B roubles (US$627M) in the Chelyabinsk region in 2012. Nonetheless, the region appears to have rebounded from the financial crisis which escalated at the end of Q3 2011, with production rising 13.7% q-o-q from Q4 2011and consumption up 8.9% for the same period. From **Nexans** ’ Q1 2012 financial repo

Demand in Southern Europe, meanwhile, continues to be subdued.  Meanwhile, **Prysmian** reported that demand from infrastructure was the most robust in Scandinavia, Eastern Europe and Italy, while the rest of Southern Europe was stable. #### Other additions to world wirerod capacity 

In India, **Airen Metals** announced plans to develop a 10,000t/y copper wirerod plant in the Shree Khatushyamji Industrial Area in Rajasthan.  The project is expected to be commissioned in December 2013. Another Indian project is currently being developed by **Citizen Metalloys** , which is constructing a 5,000t/y 8mm continuous cast wirerod plant in Ahmedabad.  Construction work is expected to be completed in 2013. The plant will exclusively supply the domestic market.

The association expects the production of copper and copper alloy semis to fall by 2.4% in 2012, to 1.0Mt, mainly attributed to poor end-use demand caused by increases in housing and value-added taxes. The products under consideration are energy-efficient air conditioners and televisions. The association also said that the nation’s inventories of air conditioners stood at 20M units at the end of 2011, around twice the normal level. - **Mueller Industries** , the US based producer of copper tube and brass products, reported a decrease in r

evenues of 16.0% y-o-y in Q1 2012.  The company attributes this loss to an extra week of business in 2011 and to lower raw material costs.  Mueller expects to perform better in the remainder of the year as it anticipates a pick-up in US construction.  The company noted that building permits for single family homes rose by 30% y-o-y in March 2012 combined with more affordable house prices and cheaper mortgages.

#### Mine Production 

- On 16<sup>th</sup> April, it was reported that production at the **Collahuasi** mine in Chile will likely fall short of its target for 2012 due to 18-20 days of disruption in Q1 from heavy rains and snow. **Anglo American** said that Collahuasi is unlikely to make up for the loss during the year due to declining ore grades.  However, consideration has been given to boosting production by accelerating waste removal in order to access higher ore grades earlier.  The 2012 production target for the Collahuasi mine is 460,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 

- On 21<sup>st</sup> April, **Glencore** announced that its majority-owned Zambian subsidiary, **Mopani Copper Mines** , had resumed its operations after a closure due to environmental violations.  The company’s **Mufulira** heap leaching plant was ordered to cease production in March due to excessive acid mist emissions.  Last year, Mufulira produced 40,000t of copper-in-concentrate and 10,000t of EW cathode. 

- On 20<sup>th</sup> April, it was reported that operations at **Milpo** ’s **Ivan** copper mine in Chile had been suspended as a result of high production costs, which were mainly attributed to declining ore grades.  In 2011, the mine produced approximately 6,000t of EW cathode. 

- According to Peru’s Mining Federation, Peruvian miners are set to stage a one-day general strike on 14<sup>th</sup> May in protest against dismissals of workers at operations owned by **Empresa Siderurgica del Peru SAA** and **Shougang Corp** .  The miners are also protesting against the proposed shutdown of **Renco Group** ’s zinc smelter. 

- A crusher failure occurred at **Hillgrove Resources’ Kanmantoo** copper mine in Australia.  The company reported on 28<sup>th</sup> March that throughput at the mill had to be reduced by 40,000t/d, down to 160,000t/d in March.   Full milling capacity of 200,000t/d is expected to resume in April.  The company believes that the lost production can be recovered during the course of 2012.  Kanmantoo is expected to produce 16,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2012 and increase production to 20,000t in 2013. 

- On 3<sup>rd</sup> April, the **Indonesian government** announced plans to implement a 25% export tax on coal and base metals this year, which may increase to 50% in 2013.  The news comes after several announcements of new mining regulations earlier this year, including a ban on exports of unprocessed metal ores from 2014.  The late

st regulation is intended to prevent a mine production boom prior to the 2014 ban coming into force. 

- On 30<sup>th</sup> March, the **Zambian government** announced plans to phase out the suspension of the issuance of mining licences that has been overseen since October 2011.  The suspension was imposed in order to root out suspected corruption in the process.  Issuance of rights for prospecting as well as mining rights for small scale operations have resumed immediately, but the ban on permits remains in place and is expected to be phased out gradually.

- The **Zambian government** announced on the 4<sup>th</sup> April that it intends to ban the export of copper raw materials in an effort to add value to the domestic industry.  The **Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry** sees the production of the higher value-added copper and copper products as key for reducing unemployment and boosting the local economy.  In 2008, Zambia introduced a 15% export levy on copper concentrates aimed at adding value locally.  There are three smelters situated in Zambia and in 2011 we estimate that they processed 512,000t of copper-inblister with 200,000t of this exported to China for electrorefining.  By comparison, copper-inconcentrate production amounted to 531,000t in the same period. 

- It was reported on 27<sup>th</sup> April that **Oz Minerals** remains interested in acquiring **Cupru Min SA Abrud** , which controls the **Rosia Poieni** mine in Romania.  The company is being sold through an ongoing privatisation process administered by the incumbent Romanian government as per an agreement made with the **International Monetary Fund** .  Oz Minerals was a bidder in the sale of the company which eventually broke down when the auction winner, **Roman Copper Corporation** , missed a legal deadline to sign the contract agreement. **Roman Copper Corporation** has since entered into a consortium with Canadian exploration company, **Valhalla Resources** , with the intention of acquiring the Romanian company. 

- It was announced on 24<sup>th</sup> April that **CST Mining** signed an agreement to sell its 70% stake in the **Mina Justa** copper project in Peru to **Cumbres Andinas** , a subsidiary of Peru’s **Minsur S.A.** in a deal worth US$505M.  The remaining 30% share is held by Korea’s **KORES** (15%) and **LS Nikko Copper** (15%).  Upon reaching full capacity, the project is expected to produce 62,000t of copper-in-concentrate and 52,000t of EW cathode.  We had expected start-up of the SXEW operations in late 2015 followed by commissioning of the concentrator after 2018.  The change in ownership may lead to a different development timeframe. 

#### Exploration and Development 

- On 27<sup>th</sup> April, it was reported that **Teck Resources** submitted an environmental impact assessment for its US$5.6B project to expand the **Quebrada Blanca

** mine in Chile.  The plans are aimed at adding production of 200,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate over 39 years. Construction is anticipated to begin in July 2013, with commissioning taking place in 2016.  We expect production from Quebrada Blanca will total 69,000t of EW cathode in 2012. 

- It was reported on 30<sup>th</sup> April that the **Supreme Court of Chile** upheld an earlier ruling that the environmental permit for **Goldcorp** 's **El Morro** copper-gold project is invalid.  The ruling was made on the grounds that the Chilean environmental permitting authority had not sufficiently consulted the indigenous people of an area affected by the project.  Goldcorp, who own a 70% stake in the US$3.9B project, has halted development work and does not have a view on how long it will take to resolve the environmental issues.  We anticipate that once commissioned the project would see production of 170,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate and 9,330kg/y of gold.

#### Smelting and Refining 

- On 12<sup>th</sup> April, it was reported that the restructuring plan for **Doe Run Peru** ’s 75,000t/y **La Oroya** smelter was rejected by creditors.  The US$168M investment plans aimed to restore operations at the plant after it closed in June 2009 as a result of financial difficulties and a stalled environmental cleanup.  Doe Run Peru's main creditor is the Peruvian government, with 36% of its debt, while the other major creditor is the **Renco Group** with 35%.  The plans were rejected on the grounds that they potentially rendered the Peruvian government liable for environmental lawsuits.  Doe Run Peru has 30 days to revise its restructuring plan before the board is eligible to find a new company to operate the plant or liquidate it completely. 

- On 10<sup>th</sup> April, **Yunnan Tin** said that it expects to meet its goal to begin production of its first copper smelter, based in Geiju City, China in mid-2012.  The company expects to produce 60,000t of copper cathode in 2012, half of the smelter’s 120,000t production capacity.  Copperin-concentrate

feedstock is expected to be sourced from the overseas market.
